question.problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{6x+1}$ at the point where $x=4$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=6x+1.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot 6 \\  & =\frac{6}{2\sqrt{6x+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=4} & ={(\frac{6}{2\sqrt{6x+1}})|}_{x=4} \\  & =\frac{6}{2\sqrt{6(4)+1}} \\  & =\frac{6}{2\sqrt{25}} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
